messages:
maria: Heads up — saw headroom thrash on prod lane during the 03:00 UTC spike. Continuous-batcher leases kept rebalancing and we got p99 jumps. Collecting notes here and tagging runtime folks.

aj: Any recent deploys around that time?

maria: No user-facing deploys. infra autoscaler did a small rebalance. Metrics: p50 ~12ms, p95 ~78ms, p99 ~420ms token latency for a ~2k qps tenant; throughput dropped ~18% for ~4m tokens in the window.

kevin: My first guess is lease churn + KV cache cold starts. If a batcher loses its lease it drops in-flight KV affinity and the next runner fetches weights/kv -> latency spike.

zhen: Can you share the lease config we used? default lease_ms?

maria: Current: `lease_ms: 200` (hard preempt), `heartbeat_ms: 50`, `rebalance_window_ms: 250`.

aj: 200ms seems aggressive for heavy sequences. If a lane briefly stalls (GC, io), another worker will steal and cause duplicate warmups. We should try soft leases + reservation credits first.

kevin: Agreed. Proposal: extend lease to 2s for production lanes with >1k qps and add a soft-handshake path where the stealing worker signals `intent_to_take` and waits for `grace_ms: 40` to allow KV transfer or commit of batch. Pseudocode: 
```
lease_ms=2000
grace_ms=40
if intent_to_take and owner_heartbeat within grace_ms: wait else take
```

maria: That could reduce thrash but increases worst-case stall time. We need a gating experiment.

aj: Also consider credit-based admission: keep a small per-lane token pool (headroom tokens) that are consumed on lease transfers. If tokens exhausted, new leases are delayed until tokens refill. That prevents cascade stealing.

zhen: How do tokens refill? fixed-rate or successful-stable-window? I prefer refill on stable window (no steal for X ms) to adapt to burstiness.

kevin: Refill approach: `tokens = min(max_tokens, tokens + stable_ms / refill_unit)`. Stable means owner holds lease without preemption. This gives backpressure without increasing tail.

sara: Can we simulate this in the test harness? We should reproduce lane hot-shard with synthetic per-tenant skew and an autoscaler flapping event. I can build a small scenario in `inflight-sim` next week.

maria: Yes please. Also let's add tracing hooks to surface `lease_acquire`, `lease_release`, and `intent_to_take` with trace IDs so we can correlate kv cache misses.

ops-bot: deploy-batcher-experiment branch created: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/lease-soft-handshake. PR queued for perf test.

aj: For rollout plan: 1) Canary change lease_ms->2000 for low-traffic hosts; 2) Enable soft-handshake in parallel; 3) Enable token headroom if stable. Monitor p99 and token throughput. Rollback if p99 > baseline + 15% for 10m.

kevin: Also add metric `lease_steals_per_min` and `kv_warm_start_rate`. Those will be primary signals.

maria: Next steps: sara will build sim, kevin will prototype soft-handshake, aj will draft rollout playbook. I'll collect traces and schedule a canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

zhen: +1. Also let's keep per-tenant min-lease-ms override so enterprise tenants with strict SLOs can pin smaller value.

aj: one more thought — if we add a small prefetcher that replicates KV headers to the stealing worker during handshake, we can cut warm rates. Needs careful security review.

maria: Noted. For now let's focus on lease and token experiments. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
